data.body_html:
Imagine sipping chilled champagne on the deck of a private motor yacht as the sun sinks behind La Concha, the sky turning shades of orange and pink over the Marbella coastline. That’s exactly what you get with our Marbella sunset cruise with champagne & tapas. Departing from Puerto Banús at 19:30, this 2-hour escape is priced from €749 for up to 11 guests aboard the Azimut 39 or Astondoa 40. All you need to do is show up – we handle the skipper, the bubbles, and the Spanish bites.

What’s included in your Marbella sunset cruise

The price covers everything except your transport to the port. Here’s the full list:

  • Licensed skipper – experienced, English-speaking, handles all navigation
  • Champagne or cava – one bottle per booking, served chilled
  • Spanish tapas – jamón ibérico, manchego cheese, olives, pan con tomate
  • Unlimited drinks – soft drinks, water, beer, white wine
  • Fuel & insurance – no hidden extras
  • 21% IVA (VAT) – legally required, already in the price

No need to pack a cooler or worry about hidden fees. The boat is yours for the full 2 hours.

The boats: Azimut 39 & Astondoa 40

Two well-maintained 12.5-metre motor yachts handle this cruise. The Azimut 39 sleeps 11 guests comfortably, while the Astondoa 40 takes up to 9. Both have spacious aft cockpits for tapas and forward sunbeds for watching the sunset. Top speed is around 28 knots, but we cruise gently at 8-10 knots to keep the ride smooth and the champagne upright.

The sunset route: Puerto Banús to the Golden Mile

We leave the marina at 19:30 and head west along the coast. You’ll pass the mansions of the Golden Mile, the outline of La Concha, and the beaches of Marbella. The skipper will anchor briefly near Río Verde or Cala del Faro so you can toast the sunset with the engine off. The return leg runs past Puerto Banús’s superyacht row as the lights come on.

If the sea is calm, you might spot dolphins – they’re common in the Bay of Marbella during summer evenings. The whole cruise covers roughly 10-12 nautical miles at a leisurely pace.

Why a sunset cruise works in Marbella

Marbella’s south-facing coast means the sun sets directly over the sea from May to September. Air temperatures in summer hover around 28-32°C at 19:30, dropping to a pleasant 24°C by 21:30. The water temperature in July and August reaches 24-26°C – warm enough for a quick dip if you fancy a swim stop.

Puerto Banús itself is a spectacle at dusk: the luxury boutiques, the floating gin palaces, the buzz of the terrace bars. Your cruise gives you the best seat in the house – on the water, looking back at it all.

How to book your sunset cruise

Booking is straightforward. Reserve online or message us on WhatsApp. We’ll confirm availability for the Azimut 39 or Astondoa 40 within 2 hours. Payment secures the slot. The meeting point is Puerto Banús – exact berth sent after booking. Arrive 15 minutes early for a 19:30 departure.

If you want a longer cruise – say 3 or 4 hours to reach Cabopino or Estepona at sunset – just ask. Pricing is on request via WhatsApp.

What to bring (and what not to bring)

  • Bring: sunglasses, sunscreen, a light jacket or sweater (sea breeze after sunset), your phone for photos
  • Don’t bring: your own alcohol (we’ve got it covered), glass bottles (we provide glassware), large bags (space is limited)

The boat has a small cooler for your personal items. Leave valuables ashore.

Frequently asked questions

The sunset cruise departs at 19:30 from Puerto Banús. This timing lets you catch the golden hour over the Mediterranean and watch the sun dip behind La Concha. Return is around 21:30.

We use the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, up to 9 guests) or the Azimut 39 (12.5m, up to 11 guests). Both are well-suited for sunset cruising with spacious sundecks and aft cockpits. Prices start at €749 for 2 hours.

You don’t need to – the charter includes champagne, tapas, soft drinks, beer, cava and white wine. If you have specific dietary requirements, let us know at booking and we can adjust the tapas selection.

Is this a private charter?

Yes, every sunset cruise is a private charter – just your group and the skipper. You won’t share the boat with strangers. The boat is yours for the 2-hour window.

Meet at Puerto Banús – we’ll send the exact pontoon and berth number after booking. Arrive 15 minutes early. There’s paid parking nearby or you can take a taxi to the port.

Can we extend the cruise beyond 2 hours?
